relations.statement: Stone uniqueness applies to the entire specified group, not one sample.
Integer spectral shifts agree at all integer sample times.
Dyadic compatibility gives representative-independent multiplication on the dense subgroup.
Continuous dense-time extensions, when they exist, are unique by density.
A fixed finite-dimensional energy branch selects a unique logarithm.
Positive determinant is necessary for a finite real matrix exponential; it is not sufficient for rate embeddability.
